items.title: Cline v4.1.26
items.summary: Added Cloud tasks: Settings > API Configuration has a Local | Cloud toggle when cloud sessions are on. Cloud picks the Cline model new cloud tasks run on, saved separately from your local models. Clicking the model label in a cloud session's composer opens it…
items.html:
Added
  • Cloud tasks: Settings > API Configuration has a Local | Cloud toggle when cloud sessions are on. Cloud picks the Cline model new cloud tasks run on, saved separately from your local models. Clicking the model label in a cloud session's composer opens it there.
  • Starting or resuming a cloud sandbox shows a progress card with the repo, branch and steps (start sandbox, clone repository, start agent). It collapses once the agent starts.
Changed
  • Cloud sessions hide the Plan/Act toggle and the auto-approve bar instead of showing them disabled.
  • With no model chosen, the Cline provider uses Claude Sonnet 5.5 again, which is back at the top of Cline's recommended list.
  • Model requests retry at most 3 times instead of 5.
  • Kimi K3 now gets max reasoning for Extra High and Max, instead of an xhigh setting it rejects.
  • Refreshed the model catalog. Adds the CommandCode, Reflection, Liquid Inference and Munito AI providers and drops CrofAI, iFlow and Llama. The Cline free list adds Reflection Beam, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and Laguna S 2.1 and drops Mimo V2.6 Flash and Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor. ClinePass now defaults to Kimi K3.1 Pro and adds MiniMax M3.1 Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017. Default models change for most other providers, mostly to Kimi K3.1 Pro, MiniMax M3.1 Flash or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017. If you use a provider without pinning a model, expect a different default.
Fixed
  • GPT-6 models (such as gpt-6-sol and gpt-6.1-sol) work on OpenAI and Azure OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and SAP AI Core no longer rejects requests with "Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens'". Both now get max_completion_tokens.
  • Gemini API keys (the gemini provider) no longer send native Google Search. Free-tier keys failed every turn with a 429 quota error on Gemini 3+, and on Gemini 2.x every Cline tool was dropped.
  • Toggling Plan/Act while a task is starting no longer drops your first prompt, and the session no longer keeps running with the other mode's tools.
  • Disabled rules stay disabled.
  • Starting a command no longer moves keyboard focus into the terminal, so text you're typing in the chat no longer lands in the shell.
  • Cancelling a task or opening another one while Cline is asking a question no longer lets your next message get taken as the answer to the old question.
  • A turn whose connection drops after the model has streamed only reasoning is now retried instead of ending the task.
  • Auto-compaction no longer runs for models with an unknown context limit, and it no longer runs again every few tool calls after the first compaction.
  • ask_question: the model keeps going after you pick an option, and empty answers are rejected.
  • run_commands with an empty command list now returns an error instead of a silent success. On PowerShell, the tool tells the model how quote escaping works and to confirm recursive deletes first.
  • Task header badges wrap instead of hiding the close button, the GitHub connection check no longer flashes a loading indicator, and the Local/Cloud toggle's padding is fixed.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/cline/cline/compare/v4.1.25...v4.1.26

items.title: Cline v4.1.25
items.summary: Added Cline Cloud sessions, rolling out gradually: run a task in a hosted sandbox on a GitHub repo and branch you pick. Turn it on in Settings. Cloud tasks show in Recent and History with their status, notify you when they finish, and keep running after you…
items.html:
Added
  • Cline Cloud sessions, rolling out gradually: run a task in a hosted sandbox on a GitHub repo and branch you pick. Turn it on in Settings. Cloud tasks show in Recent and History with their status, notify you when they finish, and keep running after you close your editor.
Changed
  • With no model chosen, the Cline provider now uses Gemini 4 Argon, the new first model in Cline's recommended list. OpenRouter stays on Claude Sonnet 5.5.
  • Refreshed the model catalog. Adds the Boundless and Standard Compute providers, and SambaNova now comes from the catalog with MiniMax M3 as its default. The Cline recommended list adds Gemini 4 Argon and drops Grok 4.7, and the Cline free list replaces Step 5 Preview with Nemotron 3.5 Super VL. OpenCode Go no longer lists MiniMax M2.7. Default models change for Cortecs, CrossModel, Eden AI, Google Gemini, GitHub Copilot, Google Vertex AI, LLM Gateway, Ofox, OpenCode Go, and Prime Inference (Gemini 4 Argon), Fireworks AI, Nebius Token Factory, and Requesty (Muse Spark Open), CoreWeave, DigitalOcean, NanoGPT, and Nvidia (Nemotron 3.5 Super VL), Aixy and Neon (Claude Haiku 5.5), Agnes AI, Ambient, IteraCompute, Poe, Scaleway, and SenseNova. If you use one of those providers without pinning a model, expect a different default.
Fixed
  • Long requests to local models (LM Studio, Ollama) no longer fail after 5 minutes of silence with terminated: BodyTimeoutError while the server is still processing a large prompt.
  • OpenAI Compatible base URLs are used exactly as entered. A host-only URL like https://abc.com used to get /v1 added silently. Host-only URLs saved by earlier versions get /v1 added once, so existing setups keep working.
  • Images and files attached to an answer to one of Cline's questions now reach the model instead of being dropped.
  • When a provider error interrupts a response mid-stream, Cline retries it up to 3 times before failing the turn.
  • In JetBrains, the Run task card stays above the Auto-approve bar.
  • Auto Compact and its strategy setting sit together again in Feature settings.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/cline/cline/compare/v4.1.24...v4.1.25

items.title: Cline v4.1.24
items.summary: Changed With no model chosen, the Cline and OpenRouter providers now use Claude Sonnet 5.5. For Cline, that's the first model in Cline's recommended list. Selecting ai& shows its own API key and model picker, instead of the generic OpenAI-compatible form with…
items.html:
Changed
  • With no model chosen, the Cline and OpenRouter providers now use Claude Sonnet 5.5. For Cline, that's the first model in Cline's recommended list.
  • Selecting ai& shows its own API key and model picker, instead of the generic OpenAI-compatible form with base URL and custom headers.
  • Refreshed the model catalog. Adds Claude Haiku 5.5 and the AI/ML API, LowRouter, and Prime Inference providers. The Cline free list adds Step 5 Preview. The v0 provider now offers only its default model, v0-1.5-md, and OpenCode Go uses its new https://opencode.ai/inference/go/v1 endpoint. Default models change for 302.AI, Cortecs, CrossModel, DevPass, DigitalOcean, Eden AI, GitHub Copilot, Google Vertex AI, LLM Gateway, Meta, Moark, NanoGPT, NEAR AI Cloud, Neuralwatt, Novita AI, Ofox, OpenCode Go, Requesty, Vivgrid, and a few others (most now Claude Haiku 5.5 or Muse Wonder 1.0). If you use one of those providers without pinning a model, expect a different default.
Fixed
  • Turning reasoning off no longer fails with a 400 error on GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Fable 5 or Claude Opus 5.5, and now works on every provider. Level-only Gemini models no longer reject the request with a thinking-budget error.
  • An MCP server or hook that exits before reading all of its input no longer crashes the extension host about 3 seconds later.
  • A 404 from a stale or retired model id is no longer shown as a sign-in problem. Cline shows the real error instead of the logged-out card.
  • Errors in the Cline output log keep their details. Production builds used to drop them, so a line like "Cline OAuth login failed:" showed no reason.
  • Deleting a slash command from the input keeps the spacing of the text around it.
  • Screenshots and other images no longer inflate the token estimate, which made auto-compaction run long before the conversation was near its limit.
  • Auto-compaction uses the selected model's context window when the catalog entry has none.
  • Rule files that are symlinks now load, and skills in .claude/skills are now discovered.
  • The editor tool no longer receives null in place of the text to replace from some models.
  • Settings migrated from older versions no longer add an empty SAP AI Core provider.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/cline/cline/compare/v4.1.23...v4.1.24

items.title: Cline v4.1.23
items.summary: Changed If a model's response ends without a recognized finish reason, Cline asks it to continue once instead of treating the response as complete. Refreshed the model catalog. The Cline recommended list adds GPT-6.1 Sol, and the free list adds Solar Mini 4…
items.html:
Changed
  • If a model's response ends without a recognized finish reason, Cline asks it to continue once instead of treating the response as complete.
  • Refreshed the model catalog. The Cline recommended list adds GPT-6.1 Sol, and the free list adds Solar Mini 4 and drops DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and space-bunny-alpha. Default models change for 302.AI, AKI.IO, Blue Claw, CoralBricks, CrossModel, DevPass, DigitalOcean, GMI Cloud, LLM Gateway, Mistral, NanoGPT, Neon, Nvidia, Ofox, Requesty, Subconscious, The Grid AI, Vivgrid, and Vultr. Vultr's model ids were renamed upstream, so a pinned Vultr model may need to be re-selected. If you use one of those providers without pinning a model, expect a different default.
Fixed
  • Generate Commit Message now follows your .clinerules, so conventions like language, format, and ticket references apply to commit messages too.
  • Claude through a custom Anthropic base URL (Azure AI Foundry, corporate gateways) no longer fails with a 400 error. 4.1.22 started sending an option only Anthropic's own API accepts.
  • Kimi K3 and other models that only accept certain reasoning levels no longer reject requests. Cline picks the closest level the model supports.
  • When an MCP tool returns more output than fits in context, Cline can now read the rest. It gets a preview plus a link it can page through with read_files, so the output past the cutoff is no longer lost.
  • Approve and Reject on a tool approval work right away, even while the panel is still updating. A late update failure no longer rejects a later, unrelated approval.
  • Old tasks no longer show leftover Focus Chain checklist rows when reopened.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/cline/cline/compare/v4.1.22...v4.1.23

items.title: Cline v4.1.22
items.summary: Added New providers: Bee (by HEOSSI) and Pareto Inference (PARETO_API_KEY). Changed Direct Anthropic requests now use Anthropic's server-side refusal fallback. On OpenRouter and Cline, Anthropic models can fail over to another upstream provider instead of…
items.html:
Added
  • New providers: Bee (by HEOSSI) and Pareto Inference (PARETO_API_KEY).
Changed
  • Direct Anthropic requests now use Anthropic's server-side refusal fallback. On OpenRouter and Cline, Anthropic models can fail over to another upstream provider instead of failing the request.
  • When a response is blocked by a content filter, Cline now says so and suggests rephrasing, instead of "Model returned empty response".
  • Refreshed the model catalog. GPT-6.1 Sol becomes the default model for OpenAI, OpenRouter, GitHub Copilot, Cortecs, Eden AI, Kilo Gateway, both LLM Gateway providers, NanoGPT, OpenCode Zen, and Requesty. Vercel AI Gateway moves to Ling 3.1 Flash, Tempr Gateway to MiMo V2.6 Flash, CrossModel and Ofox to Claude Sonnet 5.5, Pioneer to GLiNER 2.5 Decide, and Scaleway to Qwen 3.8 27B. The Cline recommended list adds Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Opus 5.5. If you use one of those providers without pinning a model, expect a different default.
Fixed
  • After an API error you can type and send a new message instead of only using Retry. A /compact (or /smol, /newtask) typed during recovery stays in the composer instead of being sent to the model as text.
  • If a new task fails Cline sign-in, signing in and submitting a revised prompt now starts the task with that prompt. Before, nothing happened.
  • Reset Code is now disabled when a message has no checkpoint, and no longer stays disabled for a message whose checkpoint exists (seen on slow disks). Changing the Checkpoints setting now applies to the active task, and follow-up messages typed while it applies are kept in order.
  • Canceling right after sending a message now stops the task. A cancel that landed while the turn was still being set up was ignored, and the task kept running.
  • Reasoning tokens are no longer counted twice in token usage. Cost is unchanged.
  • Amazon Bedrock: GPT-6 and GPT-5.6 route through inference profiles, and India regions (ap-south-1, ap-south-2) resolve the in. profile. OpenAI models behind inference profiles get the reasoning effort setting they support. Nova 2 Lite with high reasoning, application inference-profile ARNs, and Nova Micro no longer get requests Bedrock rejects. A legacy AWS profile setting saved without the "use profile" flag now carries over as profile authentication instead of being dropped.
  • Gateway models on providers that mix endpoints keep their own API protocol instead of falling back to the provider-wide default.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/cline/cline/compare/v4.1.21...v4.1.22

items.title: Cline v4.1.21
items.summary: Added New provider: ai&, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving open-weight models from Japan. Changed Refreshed the model catalog to 6,386 models across 209 providers. The resolved default model changes for 19 providers that do not pin one, 11 of them to…
items.html:
Added
  • New provider: ai&, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving open-weight models from Japan.
Changed
  • Refreshed the model catalog to 6,386 models across 209 providers. The resolved default model changes for 19 providers that do not pin one, 11 of them to Claude Opus 5.5 (including GitHub Copilot and Vertex). If you use one of those providers without pinning a model, expect a different default.
  • Raised the minimum js-yaml version to 4.3.2 to pick up a security fix in the parser used to read rule and skill frontmatter.
Fixed
  • Long replies on local models (llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio) that hit the output-token limit now compact the conversation and retry once instead of ending the task. These servers cap generation at whatever context is left, regardless of the output budget you set. If compaction cannot help, the existing concise-retry recovery still runs, and the partial answer is kept.
  • Reopening a task that failed now shows the error with the retry option, instead of presenting it as a completed task.
  • A command that prints nothing no longer shows a raw JSON blob like [{"query":"git add -A","result":"","success":true}] as its output.
  • On Windows, @-mention search results now show the right file names. Nested files such as a subfolder's README rendered as /README.md, and the same open file could appear twice.
  • Canceling a request while it waits to retry an empty model response now takes effect right away, instead of after the backoff finishes.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/cline/cline/compare/v4.1.20...v4.1.21

items.title: Cline v4.1.20
items.summary: Changed Sub-agents spawned in the same step now run their tool calls at the same time rather than one after another. Tools that must run in order still do, and the parent still waits for every result before its next turn. Models that advertise a large output…
items.html:
Changed
  • Sub-agents spawned in the same step now run their tool calls at the same time rather than one after another. Tools that must run in order still do, and the parent still waits for every result before its next turn.
  • Models that advertise a large output limit now get a bigger default output budget — 30% of the limit rather than a flat 32,000 tokens, whichever is larger. Nothing changes for models under roughly 107k output tokens; longer responses can mean higher per-turn cost and latency.
  • Refreshed the model catalog: 203 to 209 providers and 6,079 to 6,237 models. Kimi For Coding splits into separate kimi.com and kimi.ai providers, and AI21 Labs, ainetcafe, Inco, OCI Generative AI, Tempr, and Vispark are new. The resolved default model changes for 36 providers that do not pin one — most landing on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM 5.3 Flash, or MiMo V2.6 Flash. If you use one of those providers without pinning a model, expect a different default.
Fixed
  • UserPromptSubmit and TaskStart hooks can inject context again. What those hooks returned as contextModification was being dropped — only cancel survived — so a hook meant to add repository facts or house rules to a task silently did nothing. The context is now delivered as a <hook_context> block on the run's first request, the same as before the regression, and the raw block never renders in the transcript. A hook also no longer receives its own previously injected text back as the next turn's prompt.
  • Unsent text in the composer survives Retry. Retry sent no composer content but still ran the same cleanup as approval actions, deleting the only copy of anything typed while a request was in flight. Text, quote context, images, and files are now tracked as one draft that only submitting actions consume.
  • Output from background commands now streams into the command row while the command runs, instead of appearing only when it finishes.
  • The Azure API version configured for a provider is now honored in tasks and mirrored to providers.json.
  • Rules are found and shown consistently. The Rules panel listed only .clinerules and the Documents global folder, so rules loaded from .cline/rules, ~/.cline/rules, or ~/Cline/Rules were applied to the model but missing from the panel — and on Windows with a OneDrive-redirected Documents folder, global rules were not found at all.
  • Deleting a task from history now actually removes it. A task whose index entry was missing but whose file on disk survived was reported as deleted and then reappeared on the next refresh.
  • Sub-agents you configure yourself no longer ask you to approve their individual tool calls after you have already approved the delegation.
  • Compaction no longer silently falls back to truncation partway through a long task. The summarizer kept the credentials captured when the task started, so once they refreshed its request failed with an authorization error that was swallowed; it now follows the task's current credentials and model.
  • A model turn that hits its output-token limit before making a tool call no longer ends the task. It is retried up to three times with a reminder to respond concisely and split large work across tool calls.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/cline/cline/compare/v4.1.19...v4.1.20

items.title: Cline v4.1.19
items.summary: Added Images attached to a model that cannot read them are now flagged instead of silently discarded. Thumbnails get a warning badge and the composer explains that the images will be ignored, with a button to switch to an image-capable model. Previously the…
items.html:
Added
  • Images attached to a model that cannot read them are now flagged instead of silently discarded. Thumbnails get a warning badge and the composer explains that the images will be ignored, with a button to switch to an image-capable model. Previously the thumbnail looked normal and the image was replaced with a text placeholder just before the request, so there was no way to tell it had been dropped. Model info and the attachment picker also report image support accurately for models that declare text-only input without listing capabilities.
Changed
  • Cline's logo and icons have been refreshed throughout the extension, including the activity bar and panel icons.
  • The W&B Inference provider is now listed as CoreWeave, with its sign-up and API-key links updated to match CoreWeave's current documentation.
Fixed
  • Long tasks now compact when they actually need to rather than running out of room. The trigger compared a character-based estimate of the conversation (~3 characters per token) against the model's context limit, so content that tokenizes far denser than that — disassembly, image dumps, minified sources — could fill the real context window while the estimate stayed under the threshold and compaction never fired; the turn was then squeezed down to a handful of output tokens. The trigger now also uses the token count the provider itself reports, and how much history is kept is scaled by how far off the estimate turned out to be. The summarizer's output budget also doubled, so a model that reasons before answering can no longer spend the whole budget thinking and return no summary at all.
  • On Windows, opening a repository that contains a file named rg.exe, git.exe, or powershell.exe no longer runs that file in place of the real program. Bare program names were resolved through the workspace directory before PATH, so a planted executable ran with your privileges as soon as the workspace was indexed. Cline now sets Windows' NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath opt-out at startup, in both the VS Code extension and the JetBrains core. Processes Cline launches inherit it, so inside a Command Prompt shell a program in the current directory now needs .\ as it already does in PowerShell.
  • A model turn that fails mid-stream with a transient provider error is now retried up to three times with backoff instead of ending the task. A single rate-limit response forwarded by a gateway previously surfaced as a failed task. A turn that has already streamed output is never retried, so nothing is duplicated.
  • Terminal commands that succeed without printing anything (git add -A on a clean tree, for example) are now reported as empty output. They were treated as a shell-integration failure, which fed the model a snapshot of unrelated terminal scrollback prefixed with a warning that the output could not be captured, so silent commands intermittently looked like failures.
  • Checkpoints no longer re-hash every untracked file on each message. In workspaces holding large untracked directories this delayed every message by seconds to minutes; a persistent per-task index now lets git skip files it has already seen.
  • run_commands no longer hangs until its timeout after a command that backgrounds a child process. The command had finished, but the backgrounded process held the output pipes open.
  • apply_patch no longer silently overwrites an existing file when the model uses "Add File" on a path that already exists. The file's contents were replaced with no error and no record of what was lost.
  • PowerShell commands the model wrapped in another powershell -Command "..." are no longer parsed twice. The outer shell consumed $_ before the inner command ran, so pipelines using it emitted an error for every item processed while still reporting success.
  • Opening your home directory as a workspace no longer drives the extension host to exhaustion. Typing an @ mention indexed every file beneath it and re-ranked the whole index on each keystroke.
  • The "Supports Images" checkbox in OpenAI Compatible model settings now stays where you put it. The checkbox rendered the last committed value, and the re-sync that arrived during the save round-trip was re-emitted as a change event that wrote the old value back over your edit.
  • The error shown to the model when an editor call omits the text to replace now names the file and explains how to recover. The previous message was terse enough that some models re-sent the identical call until the task stopped.
  • Credentials are now stripped of invisible characters when saved, not only when pasted, and the cleanup covers AWS, GCP, and SAP fields and custom header values in addition to API keys.
  • Cline Pass now defaults to a model from your subscription rather than a free one. Its model list contains both tiers and the default was whichever model was published most recently, so a subscriber who never picked a model could be left on the free tier.
  • Cline Pass and free models now show no cost rather than the underlying market price, which is not what you are billed for.
  • Model pickers now fall back to the full Recommended, Free, and Subscribed lists when the models endpoint cannot be reached. The offline fallback was a short hardcoded list with no subscription tier at all.
  • Model lists for providers sharing the built-in catalog now refresh from the live catalog, so newly published models appear without an extension update, with timeouts so an unresponsive provider endpoint cannot stall the list.
  • Claude Code and OpenCode no longer ask for an API key they never read. Both authenticate from their own local CLI's credentials, but they were treated as key-based providers; the workaround was storing a dummy key. A missing CLI on PATH now warns rather than blocking, since a configured path or bundled binary also works.
  • The OpenAI Codex (ChatGPT subscription) model list no longer offers models the backend rejects, and Codex context limits are applied to every Codex model instead of being inherited from the OpenAI API catalog, which inflated both the context budget and the usage figures derived from it.
  • Models served by OpenCode Go are now sent over the wire protocol each one actually speaks. Every model was sent over the OpenAI chat-completions adapter, so models on that endpoint speaking other protocols failed or misbehaved.
  • Task history no longer goes blank when a task spawns many subagents. Subagent rows crowded out the tasks that created them, hiding the parent task and everything older.
  • Langfuse tracing, when configured, is now limited to the Cline and Cline Pass providers. The provider was ignored, so prompts and responses sent to third-party and bring-your-own-key providers were exported too.
Changed
  • Web search is now enabled by default on models that support it, outside YOLO mode. It can still be turned off in settings, and a settings file that cannot be read leaves it disabled rather than silently on.
  • The run_commands tool description now names the PowerShell edition in use — Windows PowerShell (powershell.exe) versus PowerShell (pwsh.exe) — quotes its guidance against that executable, and tells the model to run commands directly rather than wrapping them in another shell invocation. It also no longer describes the environment as Windows when pwsh is the configured shell on macOS or Linux.
  • Refreshed the built-in model catalog. Adds four providers (Infer by Flow7, Melious, NaN, and Wallaby) and takes the catalog from 5,788 to 6,079 models. This is a wide refresh: the resolved default model changes for 44 providers, most of them landing on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash — among them Hugging Face, Fireworks, Requesty, Nebius, Cortecs, CrossModel, DigitalOcean, Eden AI, and OpenCode Go. Gemini and Vertex now resolve to Gemini 3.8 Flash, GitHub Copilot and Vivgrid to GPT-6 Astra, and NVIDIA to GLM 5.3 Flash. If you use a provider without pinning a model, expect a different default.

items.title: Cline v4.1.17
items.summary: Everything here lands through the SDK bundle, so it applies to windows running that bundle. Added ClinePass is now surfaced across the app: a card on the account page describing what the plan covers, a hint in provider settings, and a banner on the home…
items.html:
Everything here lands through the SDK bundle, so it applies to windows running that bundle.

Added
  • ClinePass is now surfaced across the app: a card on the account page describing what the plan covers, a hint in provider settings, and a banner on the home screen. Dismissed banners stay dismissed.
Fixed
  • Fixed the background Hub process ballooning in memory during long sessions. Session status updates broadcast a full copy of the conversation transcript to every connected client, so on a large task each status change shipped megabytes and could grow the process to tens of gigabytes. Snapshots now carry state only.
  • Hook scripts that fail to spawn no longer crash the extension's core process and take the running task down with them.
  • Fixed a chat render crash on malformed api_req payloads.
  • Cost estimates no longer appear in task history for subscription-billed tasks (ClinePass, ChatGPT via Codex, and Claude Code), matching the task header.
  • Pasted provider API keys are now stripped of the invisible characters clipboards smuggle in (newlines, zero-width spaces, BOM). A key corrupted that way was hidden by the masked field and rejected by the provider with a 401 indistinguishable from a genuinely wrong key. Credential rejections now say that the API key is the problem and point at its configuration, keeping the provider's raw response as a diagnostic tail.
  • Signing in to OpenAI Codex (ChatGPT subscription) now fails with a clear "port in use" error when callback port 1455 is occupied. Previously the button opened a browser to a flow whose callback could never arrive, and nothing else happened. OAuth redirect errors such as access_denied are surfaced instead of being reported as a missing authorization code.
  • A transient network failure while refreshing OpenAI Codex or OpenAI-compatible-account tokens no longer signs you out. Only a genuinely rejected refresh token now requires re-authentication.
  • Fixed tool calling being silently disabled for Dify, SAP AI Core, opencode, and Codex CLI models. Their catalog entries declare no capabilities, and the empty list was read as an authoritative denial that stripped every tool from the request.
  • Fixed images being dropped from file reads on models whose capability list is empty.
  • Restoring a checkpoint now refuses to run when commits were made after it, instead of silently knocking them off the branch where only the reflog could recover them. Chat-only restore is unaffected.
  • apply_patch now preserves a file's existing CRLF line endings.
  • Global rules are now also read from ~/Cline/Rules, which is where the Rules tab writes them on WSL and headless installs whose Documents folder resolves to the home directory.
  • An enabled but unreachable remote (SSE or streamable HTTP) MCP server no longer stalls session startup; remote connects now have a 10 second budget.
  • Aborting a task now also cancels the delegated subagents and teammates it spawned, instead of leaving their work running.
  • Langfuse tracing now works in released builds. Detection identified the OpenTelemetry provider by class name, which minification renames, so tracing silently initialized as not ready in every published build while working in development.
  • Cline provider models are now read from the live catalog, so newly published models appear without an extension update.
  • Hook execution telemetry now fires; the task id was not threaded into hook runner creation, so those events were dropped.
Changed
  • Refreshed the built-in model catalog. Adds ten providers (Bothub, OpenReason, SenseNova (China), TokenGo, TokenRouter, Vancine, Volcengine Ark, Volcengine Ark Coding Plan, above.dev, and klokintegration.se) and updates model lists and pricing throughout. This is an unusually wide refresh: the resolved default model changes for 57 providers, most consequentially Anthropic, which now resolves to Claude Fable 5.1 instead of Claude Opus 5, with Amazon Bedrock, Vertex, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Kilo Gateway, LLM Gateway, DevPass, DigitalOcean, CrossModel, Eden AI, and NanoGPT following. If you use a provider without pinning a model, expect a different default.
  • The message the model receives when you reject a tool call now names the rejected tool and reads as your decision rather than an error.

items.html:
Everything here lands through the SDK bundle, so it applies to windows running that bundle.

Fixed
  • Cost estimates are no longer shown for providers billed by a flat-rate subscription (ClinePass, ChatGPT via Codex, and Claude Code). The task header and model pricing rows rendered API-rate dollar figures that read as real charges on top of the subscription, including a flash of them on every chat-view mount while provider listings were loading.
  • Signing back in no longer moves your last-used provider off ClinePass on credential refresh.
  • Hooks now resolve their workspace from the VS Code window instead of shared global state in ~/.cline. With a second window open on another project, a workspace's .clinerules/hooks scripts were never discovered, and hook cwd and the workspace paths passed to hook scripts resolved against whatever project some other or older Cline instance last recorded.
  • New files are now created with your platform's native line endings.
  • Fixed the codebase search tool crashing on files containing a single enormous line.
  • Credentials embedded in git remote URLs are now redacted from the workspace information sent to the model, which also now carries richer workspace metadata.
  • Installing an MCP server from the marketplace no longer misreads the catalog's -- separator as part of the server command.
  • The hub's event log can no longer grow until it fills your disk.
Changed
  • The per-tool MCP auto-approve checkboxes are hidden. MCP auto-approval is governed solely by the global "Use MCP servers" toggle — the per-tool checkboxes were no-ops that implied granularity the approval path does not have.

Fixed
  • Restore tool calling for custom OpenAI-Compatible models whose capability list was inferred from convenience flags like supportsReasoning. The inferred list read as an authoritative denial and stripped every tool from the request; an explicitly authored capability list still decides.
  • Keep Hub-backed sessions intact across a Hub restart or upgrade. Clients replay the events they missed while disconnected, and the same event is no longer delivered twice when the replay and live streams overlap.

items.html:
Everything here lands through the SDK bundle, so it applies to windows running that bundle — except the last section, which is a legacy-bundle fix.

Added
  • Let models that support it generate images during a task. Generated images render inline in the conversation.
Fixed
  • Fix code actions failing with "command not found" on VS Code 1.134.
  • Fix @ file mentions breaking on paths that contain spaces.
  • Show the diff edit view for multi-line edits in files with CRLF line endings.
  • Continue the surviving session when resuming a task, instead of rebuilding it from the original task text.
  • Clear the task-scoped settings overlay when the task view is cleared or switched, so one task's overrides no longer leak into the next.
  • Honor the classic truncation range when migrating legacy tasks.
  • Preserve LiteLLM input token limits instead of overwriting them with catalog values.
  • Restore custom base URLs for Gemini, and normalize legacy host-root values so they keep working.
  • Point provider signup links at each provider's API key page instead of a generic landing page.
  • Load skill slash commands through the skills tool instead of pasting their instructions into your message, which previously delivered them twice.
  • Stop offering image, voice, and other non-chat models in chat model pickers.
  • Deliver a PreToolUse hook's contextModification to the model again, and wait for PostToolUse hooks so their output and cancel control are honored.
  • Show tool activity a provider runs itself — every tool the Claude Code provider executes inside its own session — instead of dropping it from the conversation.
  • Fix run_commands failing with ENOENT when a structured command carried a full command line with no arguments.
  • Run PowerShell commands fail-fast, so a pipeline erroring per item stops at the first error instead of flooding output and still reporting success.
  • Keep remote configuration in step with the SDK: coordinated refreshes, session gating, and a fail-closed opt-out.
Changed
  • Show the billed cost for Cline gateway usage.
  • Refresh the model catalog, which adds AMD, Arcee, Echo, Jalapeno, Kosmik, LLM Gateway, RunInfra, and SCNet as providers and updates model lists, pricing, and per-provider default models across the board.
Fixed (legacy bundle)
  • Only treat an Anthropic invalid_request_error as a context-overflow when its message says so. An unrelated invalid request (bad tool schema, oversized image, unknown model id) no longer triggers context-overflow recovery.

items.html:
Everything in this release lands through the SDK bundle, so it applies to windows running that bundle and not the legacy one. The legacy bundle is unchanged from 4.1.9.

Added
  • Let models that support it search the web during a task, with a toggle in Feature Settings to turn it on. Search calls and their results appear in the conversation and persist across reloads.
Fixed
  • Stop two Cline installations on different builds from shutting each other's Hub daemon down in a loop, which killed live sessions with an abnormal socket close. Build identity is now compared through a total order, so at most one side of a pair can decide to retire the other.
  • Leave a Hub that is still serving sessions in place instead of replacing it mid-handshake; the swap happens once it goes idle.
  • Reclaim idle plugin sandbox processes instead of leaving them running for the life of the session.
Changed
  • Refresh the model catalog, which adds Crusoe as a provider and updates model lists and per-provider default models across the board.

items.title: FuXi v0.1.8
items.summary: FuXi 0.1.8 Release Announcement Release Date: September 22, 2026 We are pleased to announce the release of FuXi 0.1.8, a major update following 0.1.7. This release introduces rate-limit banners and an official plugin marketplace mirror, and delivers systematic…
items.html:
FuXi 0.1.8 Release Announcement

Release Date: September 22, 2026

We are pleased to announce the release of FuXi 0.1.8, a major update following 0.1.7. This release introduces rate-limit banners and an official plugin marketplace mirror, and delivers systematic stabilization and refinement across session storage, the engine, permissions, Windows compatibility, and the user interface.

New Features

  • Rate-limit banners: unified rate-limit data now feeds subscription banners; usage beyond the limit is silently rolled into additional usage with clear notification.
  • Official plugin marketplace mirror: the plugin marketplace is now served from an official GCS mirror, making plugin installs more stable and reliable.

Performance

  • Smoother long-session interactions: estimated scroll offsets and zero render-time filesystem syscalls reduce a cold first frame from ~1.6s (1000 lines) to ~160ms; scrolling performance is now independent of line count.
  • Faster resume & reads: a resume reads the transcript only once (34MB: 4.6s → 0.8s); sessions larger than 5MiB are read through a precompacted fast path in 1MB sequential chunks (~4.9× on a 30MB transcript); write-side 100ms batching keeps the disk format unchanged.
  • Streaming render fix: the linkify O(n²) full-render issue is resolved (20KB single line: 278ms → 2.9ms); streaming output no longer appears non-streaming.

Sessions & Messages

  • Session storage-chain optimization: a precompact read fast path, write-side batching, and live-cache re-append are introduced (metadata such as titles and tags flush synchronously, and external SDK writes are absorbed via a 64KB tail window).
  • Message-chain integrity: parentUuid chains now fully link every participant, with automatic re-linking after forks; switching sessions no longer loses in-flight messages; a unified session UUID registry fixes the /clear cache invalidation issue.

Permissions & Security

  • Dialog & rules: the permission dialog now uses a numbered Select list; "Always Allow" clearly displays the exact rule to be persisted; low-risk file commands (mkdir/cp/mv/touch/rmdir) are relaxed to command-name prefix rules.
  • Stability & Bash safety: the whole-UI freeze caused by permission dialogs is resolved (approval sends are now non-blocking); the Bash read-only gate is hardened (backticks and newlines can no longer bypass auto-approval); permission suggestions are built once per request and differentiated by reason.

Windows Compatibility

  • Startup & rendering: when Git for Windows is missing, startup now provides installation guidance directly (no longer stuck behind the login flow); CJK console glyphs and borders adapt to terminal capabilities, resolving mojibake, tofu, and input-box jitter; subprocess output is decoded strictly as UTF-8.

Engine & Tools

  • Non-streaming fallback: on empty or interrupted streams, the current turn is automatically retried via a non-streaming request.
  • Tool-execution dedup: a tool state machine and tracker form a dedup closed loop, eliminating duplicate tool cards.
  • Tool behavior unification: Read, Write, Edit, Notebook, and PDF tools now share consistent behavior and error messages; non-standard error prefixes are removed.

UI / MCP / Misc

  • UI: the task list is deduplicated (the right sidebar is the single task surface); the plan-approval dialog fits exactly, with buttons remaining visible on long plans.
  • MCP: the command allowlist is re-seeded after configuration reloads (servers added at runtime are no longer blocked); ~/.fuxi.json global configuration is unified.

Installation & Upgrade

Installation scripts automatically fetch the latest version with integrity verification.

macOS / Linux

curl -fsSL https://downloads.fuxicode.com/bootstrap.sh | bash

Windows (PowerShell)

irm https://downloads.fuxicode.com/bootstrap.ps1 | iex

Windows (CMD)

curl -fsSL https://downloads.fuxicode.com/install.cmd -o %TEMP%\install.cmd && %TEMP%\install.cmd

Existing users can upgrade by re-running the corresponding command. For issues, please report them at https://github.com/fuxicodex/Fuxi/issues.

items.html:
FuXi 0.1.6 Release Announcement

Release Date: September 7, 2026

FuXi 0.1.6 is now available. This release focuses on core experience consistency and stability: unified session and message handling, hardened login flow, cross-platform compatibility improvements, and a number of stability fixes.

New Features

  • Unified session & message handling: chat messages are consolidated into a single message model, removing inconsistencies between multiple handling paths; message parent-child chains are preserved more completely, and partially-compacted history survives session resume.
  • Hardened login flow: cross-process token refresh is serialized to prevent token-chain failure; tokens are refreshed proactively before expiry to avoid forced re-login; login no longer times out — it waits until the user cancels.
  • Model selection validation: the /model command now validates that the selected model is supported by the current endpoint, giving clear feedback when an invalid model name is entered.

Improvements & Fixes

  • Engine: empty responses automatically retry via non-streaming requests; fixed repeated injection of external file changes and conditional memory; coordinator queue drained before every request; gateway length errors correctly recognized as context-window overflows.
  • Bash / Windows: unified command-line parsing reduces misclassification; strict UTF-8 subprocess output on Windows avoids garbled text; nested-heredoc crash fixed; startup git-bash check and working-directory exclusion added.
  • UI & Rendering: markdown rendering improvements, box-drawing table format, sidebar reasoning state and session cost, and chat lag fixed on huge content; CJK character-width handling now applies only to legacy Windows consoles.
  • Tasks / Agent: standardized task IDs and output paths; notification queue priorities (immediate / later / next); stricter stop-task conditions; agent_busy claim check.
  • Files & Search: more accurate search timeouts; staged protection for very large file reads; Grep content checks and UNC path handling fixed.
  • MCP: /mcp toggle persisted per-project; improved port allocation and lock-backoff; staged truncation for tool output.
  • Permission & Sandbox: static directory rules support subtree matching; sandbox configuration now takes effect with settings; unified session grant logic.
  • Context compaction: staged decision for file restore after compaction; improved shared-cache partial compaction.
  • Image recognition: recognition configuration is endpoint-scoped and no longer affects the main model's vision judgment; recognition-model refusals are never cached.

Installation / Upgrade

Installation scripts fetch the latest version automatically with integrity verification.

Windows (PowerShell)

irm https://fuxicode.com/install.ps1 | iex

Windows (CMD)

curl -fsSL https://fuxicode.com/install.cmd -o %TEMP%\install.cmd && %TEMP%\install.cmd

macOS (x64 / ARM64)

curl -fsSL https://fuxicode.com/install.sh | bash

Linux (x64 / ARM64)

curl -fsSL https://fuxicode.com/install.sh | bash

Existing users can upgrade by re-running the corresponding command. For issues, please report them at https://github.com/fuxicodex/Fuxi/issues.

items.summary: FuXi 0.1.2 Release Announcement Release Date: August 6, 2026 FuXi 0.1.2 is now available, with major improvements across multi-window coordination, image capabilities, and the plugin ecosystem. New Features Multi-window coordination: switch seamlessly between…
items.html:
FuXi 0.1.2 Release Announcement

Release Date: August 6, 2026

FuXi 0.1.2 is now available, with major improvements across multi-window coordination, image capabilities, and the plugin ecosystem.

New Features

  • Multi-window coordination: switch seamlessly between concurrent sessions without interrupting your current work.
  • Image captioning: non-vision models can now generate image descriptions automatically, enabled by default.
  • Vision capability is automatically detected from known provider capabilities, with no manual configuration required.
  • Thinking mode now adapts to the task type for smarter responses.
  • Tool-level thinking has been refined, and status blink for collapsed groups in the TUI is restored.
  • Voice capture and browser tools are now integrated through the native extension bridge.

Improvements & Fixes

  • Unified MCP plugin lifecycle: plugins from manifest, channel declarations, session plugins, and other sources all load under one consistent contract.
  • Multiple security hardening improvements: plaintext MCP tokens removed, OAuth credentials scoped to their trust domains, plugin secrets kept out of prompts, and plugin reloads no longer expose stale state.
  • Path traversal is blocked before normalization, preventing path escape risks.
  • Memory extraction now runs asynchronously, with an optimized memory_saved card.
  • Model cache isolation stays stable across sessions, and compacted context remains consistent across TUI turns.
  • Each model gets a stable user identity, and long prompts are preserved intact across the OpenAPI boundary.
  • Plugin LSP lifecycle options are supported, and usable LSP plugins are recommended after real file edits.
  • Fixed empty tool results being lost before transcript replay.

Installation / Upgrade

Installation scripts fetch the latest version automatically with integrity verification.

Windows (PowerShell)

irm https://releases.fuxicode.com/bootstrap.ps1 | iex

Windows (CMD)

curl -fsSL https://releases.fuxicode.com/install.cmd -o %TEMP%\install.cmd && %TEMP%\install.cmd

macOS (Intel / Apple Silicon)

curl -fsSL https://releases.fuxicode.com/bootstrap.sh | bash

Linux (x64 / ARM64)

curl -fsSL https://releases.fuxicode.com/bootstrap.sh | bash

items.summary: FuXi 0.1.1 Release Announcement Release Date: August 6, 2026 FuXi 0.1.1 has been released. This release includes the following changes. New Features Remote Control: support for CCR v2 sessions with secure worker credential exchange and real-time event…
items.html:
FuXi 0.1.1 Release Announcement

Release Date: August 6, 2026

FuXi 0.1.1 has been released. This release includes the following changes.

New Features

  • Remote Control: support for CCR v2 sessions with secure worker credential exchange and real-time event streaming, synchronized with the local TUI
  • Remote input integrated with the local session; slash commands and prompts processed under unified security policies
  • Image preprocessing upgraded: automatic resizing and compression before upload, using the Lanczos3 scaling kernel
  • Built-in file search tools (bfs/ugrep) with no additional dependencies, available on Windows, macOS, and Linux
  • Chrome integration dialog, enabled by default
  • @mention content delivered directly to the model
  • Bash cards expanded by default
  • Exit-word routing and automatic detection of long-running task keywords

Improvements & Fixes

  • Optimized context compaction and tool result budgeting for more stable long-conversation streaming
  • Fixed Windows path conversion, snapshot, hooks, and permission rule issues
  • Fixed deepseek-v4 output limits and API request parameters (top_p)
  • Token refresh interval extended to 6 hours
  • Fixed attachment ordering, message boundaries, and hook completion order
  • Improved WebSocket 401 auto-recovery mechanism

Installation / Upgrade

Installation scripts fetch the latest version automatically with integrity verification.

Windows (PowerShell)

irm https://releases.fuxicode.com/bootstrap.ps1 | iex

Windows (CMD)

curl -fsSL https://releases.fuxicode.com/install.cmd -o %TEMP%\install.cmd && %TEMP%\install.cmd

macOS (Intel / Apple Silicon)

curl -fsSL https://releases.fuxicode.com/bootstrap.sh | bash

Linux (x64 / ARM64)

curl -fsSL https://releases.fuxicode.com/bootstrap.sh | bash

Existing users can upgrade by re-running the corresponding command. For issues, please report at: https://github.com/fuxicodex/Fuxi/issues

items.title: Cleanyourtv App v0.4.6.1 — Clean Your TV
items.summary: Clean Your TV app 0.4.6.1 fixes one thing: reconnecting to a TV that got a new Wi-Fi address. The problem After a TV software update, or on a mesh Wi-Fi, a TV can get a new address. The app only tried the address it saved the first time, so Manage stayed…
items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.4.6.1 fixes one thing: reconnecting to a TV that got a new Wi-Fi address.

The problem

After a TV software update, or on a mesh Wi-Fi, a TV can get a new address. The app only tried the address it saved the first time, so Manage stayed "Offline" and waited for the TV forever, even with debugging switched on.

The fix

When the saved address doesn't answer, the app looks for the same TV on your Wi-Fi, the way "Add a TV" does, and saves its new address. It checks it's really your TV first (the TV must recognise this phone and have the same ID), so it never connects to another TV, and a TV that already trusted your phone doesn't ask you to allow it again.

Nothing else changes from 0.4.6.

Install

Download cleanyourtv-0.4.6.1.apk below and open it on your phone (Android 9 or newer, on the same Wi-Fi as the TV). It installs over 0.4.6 and keeps everything. If you're on the 0.4.7-beta1 test build, you already have this fix.

Verify

  • SHA-256: b18e24e478d0ab47a31244cb3a1984229dde53b163ebe7758e26bcb8bfc105e1
  • Signer certificate SHA-256: eaf7af3867bb29ff4bb038854842c93f42ffe4198a087e611cb18f925201cd65 (the same key as every release)
  • Reproducible: the unsigned build is dc5180a494df1311e8b7802e4a9aadd45695f9d7a420dbae16d5fae018d04cee, the same from two clean builds.

items.title: Cleanyourtv App v0.4.6 — Clean Your TV
items.summary: Clean Your TV app 0.4.6 gives Xiaomi and Redmi TVs on Google's Android TV home the new home screen, adds a one-tap "Report a problem" button, and makes the home screen switch safer, with fixes that came straight from testers' reports. What's new The new home…
items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.4.6 gives Xiaomi and Redmi TVs on Google's Android TV home the new home screen, adds a one-tap "Report a problem" button, and makes the home screen switch safer, with fixes that came straight from testers' reports.

What's new

  • The new home screen on Xiaomi and Redmi TVs on Android 9, 10 and 11 that have no list of their own, such as the Mi TV 4i. Their setup wizard stays on and your Wi-Fi isn't touched. A Xiaomi TV with a home screen app you installed yourself gets it too, and your app stays installed.
  • Report a problem on every stop, timeout, paused change and connect problem. One tap opens a ready-filled GitHub issue in your browser, so there's nothing to paste. The app itself still sends nothing: nothing is public until you post it.
  • Run Setup again. If an earlier version left your home screen alone, for example before your TV had a list of its own, Manage now says so and offers to run Setup again.
  • Honest reasons. When another home screen app or a vendor service is why the app left the home screen alone, Setup and Manage say exactly that.

Safer home screen switch

  • TVs where a vendor service also answers the Home button keep their own home screen. One such TV failed to start after its home screen was switched in a test build.
  • On Xiaomi TVs, Mi TV+ and PatchWall's web content stay on while PatchWall stays on, because PatchWall can open at start-up. If an earlier version switched them off, Setup switches them back on before it changes the home screen.
  • Each time you open Manage, the app checks the Home button again and tells you if the TV's setup wizard could take it.
  • Right after the switch, if the TV brings up Live TV in front of the new home screen, the app presses Home again for you.

Fixes

  • Manage, the Restore point page and Done all show the restore point that "Undo everything" goes back to.
  • Manage no longer stays on "Working" after "Stop and undo".
  • Reports fold repeated connection retries into one line, so more of what happened fits.
  • The home screen switch no longer stops before it starts when the TV's screenshot is large (a 4K screen, or a detailed wallpaper). A safety check refused screenshots over 2 MB, nothing was changed, and the old home screen came back after a restart. Reports now also say which check stopped a switch, and why the TV refused a step.

Known issue

  • On some TVs (seen on Xiaomi and TCL with Android 11, and Android 14 boxes) Android doesn't let the app copy the look and wallpaper into the new home screen. The new home screen works with its default look, nothing else changes, and the fix comes in 0.4.7.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

Install

Download cleanyourtv-0.4.6.apk below and open it on an Android 9 or newer phone with a screen lock, on the same Wi-Fi as your Android TV, Google TV or Fire TV. It installs over any earlier version, including the 0.4.6 test builds, and keeps everything. If the app opens Manage for your TV, tap Run Setup again to use what's new.

Verify

  • SHA-256: a648dbd977e6b653c7ae7ad521d938102184f89b293add08dc1cd2c13f2cafa2
  • Signer certificate SHA-256: eaf7af3867bb29ff4bb038854842c93f42ffe4198a087e611cb18f925201cd65 (apksigner verify --print-certs cleanyourtv-0.4.6.apk)
  • Reproducible: the unsigned build is 5d877ced402f48795b55e7e04e8f5d518c998db50e096d4bf2a654f37e1e27ac, the same from two clean builds; scripts/verify-release.sh checks that this APK is that build plus a signature.
  • Commit 6dbb574a, upstream Clean Your TV b06ab21 (home screen 3.0).

Credits

A community-built phone app for Clean Your TV by Gathin, used with his permission. The home screen and the TV lists come from Clean Your TV and its community. Thank you to the 53 people who tested the app on their own TVs this week: every fix above started with one of your reports.

items.summary: Clean Your TV app 0.4.5 brings the 3.0 home screen from Gathin's Clean Your TV, more choices in the Look sheet, 25 more TV lists (173 in all), and fixes for phones on Android 9 to 12 that could not connect to a new TV. What's new Home screen 3.0. A TV that has…
items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.4.5 brings the 3.0 home screen from Gathin's Clean Your TV, more choices in the Look sheet, 25 more TV lists (173 in all), and fixes for phones on Android 9 to 12 that could not connect to a new TV.

What's new

  • Home screen 3.0. A TV that has the home screen from an earlier version sees "Update the home screen" in Manage. Nothing changes until you tap it, and the update keeps your look, your dock and your remote buttons.
  • More Look options on home screen 3.0: every app in one row, a dock with no band, the greeting on or off, the date under the clock, a brighter date, a warning colour on the Wi-Fi icon when the internet is down, app tiles as icons on cards, and a rim or halo highlight. The preview shows each one before anything reaches the TV, and looks you already sent stay exactly as they are.
  • 25 more TV lists from Clean Your TV, among them NVIDIA SHIELD TV (2017), Philips Google TV TA1 and TA7, Sony BRAVIA VU1 and VU3, TCL G08 (EU, Android 12), OnePlus TV (Cebu and Dosa), Xiaomi Mi Box S (Android 12) and several Xiaomi Mi TVs. The Sony BRAVIA BF1 list now matches BF1 sets, and lists we already had got their contributors' fixes.
  • Better back on. If this app switched off something a TV's list now keeps on, like a TCL remote's mic service, Manage says so and offers to switch it back on.
  • PatchWall on Xiaomi TVs is now your choice, so the remote's PatchWall button keeps working.

Fixes

  • Phones on Android 9 to 12 can connect to a new TV again. The TV never showed Allow and the app said "unreachable". Saving a restore file on phones below Android 15 is fixed too.
  • Some TCL Smart TV Pro sets on Google TV got a list made for the Android TV version, so the app left their home screen alone. They now get the right set.
  • Connection errors say what went wrong instead of "unreachable". A TV that leaves the Wi-Fi mid-run pauses the run instead of hanging.
  • "Try again" after a home screen check that timed out now really tries again, and the last screen says honestly when the home screen stayed.
  • Safer undo: "Undo everything" is no longer refused for protected apps, never switches accessibility on, and never treats a chooser screen as your home screen.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

Install

Download cleanyourtv-0.4.5.apk below and open it on an Android 9 or newer phone with a screen lock, on the same Wi-Fi as your Android TV, Google TV or Fire TV. It installs over any earlier version and keeps everything.

items.summary: Clean Your TV app 0.4.0 brings a new Look sheet for your TV's home screen: pick a picture, one of five styles and how many apps sit in a row, and see your own TV in a preview before anything reaches it. What's new Five styles, each shown as a small preview of…
items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.4.0 brings a new Look sheet for your TV's home screen: pick a picture, one of five styles and how many apps sit in a row, and see your own TV in a preview before anything reaches it.

What's new

  • Five styles, each shown as a small preview of your TV with your picture: Classic (a dark dock, a big name and a soft glow), Glass (a frosted dock and light in each app's colour), Spotlight (a big banner of the app you are on, with the app's colour across the top), All apps (every app in one grid) and Calm (no glow and no big name, just apps and your picture).
  • Pictures for any style: Mist, Aurora, Navy, Autumn lake, Curtains, Mountains (with a sky that changes with the hour), Lamp light, Neon, Cobalt, no picture, or your own photo, cropped on the phone. Diwali is there until 10 November, with its lamps and festive icons. The pictures are our own work, free to use (CC0).
  • 4 to 8 apps in a row. Fewer apps means bigger tiles. "Names under every app" puts each app's name under its tile, easier to read from the sofa.
  • More options: how the highlight moves (Lively, Smooth, Quick or Off), the big name, the glow, a ring in the app's colour, the dock band (solid, see-through or glass), the buttons at the top and a green Wi-Fi icon. Advanced has lift and zoom, see-through amount, sky strength and the settings file itself.
  • Nothing is sent until you tap "Put it on the TV". "Undo changes" takes the sheet back to how it opened, and "Put back the earlier look" brings back the look the TV had before your last send.
  • Your dock keeps its order when you go to fewer apps in a row, and empty spaces stay empty on the TV.
  • Setup's Look step is the same sheet, with Done at the bottom.
  • A look you picked before this version stays on the TV exactly as it is until you send a new one.
  • TCL: picking TCL under "Change model" now asks whether the TV's menus are in English (or your language) or in Chinese, so TCL TVs sold outside China get the right steps to connect.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

Install

What's new

    • Amazon Fire TV AFTDEC012E (#65, #76)

    • Xiaomi Mi Box 3 (#199, #224, #273)
    • Xiaomi MiTV-MFTR0 (#193, #249)
    • Xiaomi TV S Mini LED 75 2025 (#128)
    • Xiaomi Mi TV P1 43 (#184)
    • Xiaomi MiTV-MSSP1 (#57, #58, #78, #176)

    The Fire TV AFTDEC012E, the MiTV-MFTR0 and the Chromecast with Google TV HD get the clean-up and keep their own home screen: Fire OS keeps its Home, the app does not know the MFTR0's China home screen, and on the Chromecast the switch would cost casting after every reboot.

  • Updated lists. Ten lists changed upstream and follow it, among them the Hisense SmartTV 4K FFM, the Sony BRAVIA 4K UR2 and VH2, the TCL G05 and G09 Google TV and the Xiaomi TV A Pro 2026. The Xiaomi MiTV-AESP0 list keeps its setup wizard on, as in 0.3.6. Hisense TVs without an exact list also switch off Google partner setup and Calendar sync.

  • The home screen app 2.7. With its default settings the TV looks as before, with fixes: the network pill shows the VPN badge right away, the dock's corners follow its tiles, Launcher settings changes apply when you leave with Home, and the quick settings no longer crash on Android 8.0. It also speaks Ukrainian. Its new options are all off by default; the app lets you choose them in a later version. A TV set up with an earlier version is offered "Update the home screen" in Manage.

  • More apps that are never switched off. By any list, also during the home screen switch: vendor setup wizards (OnePlus, Xiaomi and Android's device provisioning), vendor home screens (Haier, OnePlus), TalkBack and Google's text-to-speech, the Sony accessibility tutorial and the TCL hearing aid, the remote's services (the Google TV remote service and its logger, Sony remote start and the OnePlus remote diagnosis), the Xiaomi TV service and TCL Live. items.title: Cleanyourtv App v0.3.6 — Clean Your TV
items.summary: Clean Your TV app 0.3.6 fixes TVs that got stuck after a home screen switch rolled back and the install that kept saying the TV stopped answering. Thank you to everyone who sent a report and a log: each of these fixes starts from one. What's new No more stuck…
items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.3.6 fixes TVs that got stuck after a home screen switch rolled back and the install that kept saying the TV stopped answering. Thank you to everyone who sent a report and a log: each of these fixes starts from one.

What's new

  • No more stuck Setup after a rollback. When the home screen switch rolled back, Setup offered "Try with the wizard off", which saved a choice that every later plan refused, and Back led to Welcome instead of the TV's restore options. That card is gone, saved choices the TV would refuse are dropped before planning, and Back on a refused plan opens Manage for a TV this app already changed (#375, #385).
  • No more endless "TV stopped answering" during an install. Some TVs end the app's install with an error while staying connected. The app now checks whether the install landed: done if it did, otherwise that step fails and Setup carries on with the clean-up, without the home screen switch (#80, #364, #367).
  • A heads-up on TCL Google TV. Before the switch, the plan screen and Manage > Home screen say that the remote's Settings (gear), Netflix and YouTube buttons don't work with the new home screen, and that Use the TV's own home screen brings them back (#275).
  • A stricter safety rule for the setup wizard. The home screen switch is never planned while the TV shows a setup wizard that can take the Home button and the switch would leave it on, also on TVs with an exact list such as the Sony BRAVIA BF1. Those TVs get the clean-up alone. The TCL G10 Google TV list switches the wizard off as part of the switch, so it keeps its switch.
  • Reports list what was switched off. The problem report now has "Switched off by this app", so a reply can say exactly what to put back.
  • Better logs, and Copy error. The diagnostics log now says why a connection failed, what the TV showed when the home check rolled back, and the step the switch stopped at. When the TV answers but the phone can't connect, the door says what on the phone can block the app (a per-app network limit on MIUI or Samsung, a VPN, Private DNS, mobile data) and offers Copy error: a short summary with no addresses in it, ready to paste into an issue.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

Install

Download cleanyourtv-0.3.6.apk below and open it on an Android 9 or newer phone with a screen lock, on the same Wi-Fi as your Android TV, Google TV or Fire TV. It installs over any earlier version and keeps everything.

items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.3.5 gives more TVs a careful clean-up and adds a safety guard for the ACER R4G. Thank you to everyone who sent a TV report: the list of apps in each one showed us what is safe to switch off on TVs nobody has tested yet.

What's new

  • More TVs get a careful clean-up. TVs from brands with one or two tested lists (Skyworth, SHARP, onn, OnePlus, Haier and others) now switch off up to six hidden feedback and advertising services: Google Feedback and its consent prompt, the print service, and Android's on-device advertising, ad personalization and ad model services. Before, these TVs got no clean-up unless a list matched the exact model (#89, #108, #169, #194, #196, #251).
  • Nothing else changes on those TVs. The home screen decision is the same as before, and the app still checks each switch-off on the TV before it runs it. TVs that already had a brand set get nothing new.
  • A safety guard for the ACER R4G. It is made by MOKA, in the same family as the TVs whose setup wizard comes back at every restart, so Setup never offers the home screen switch on it and does the clean-up alone (#74, #102).
  • Reports say which set was used. A TV report from one of these TVs now says Profile: brand set <Brand> instead of none.

items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.3.4 fixes "plan refused" on TVs whose home screen was already changed by another tool, and makes Setup honest when it can't make a safe plan. Thank you to everyone who sent a report with the log: it showed us exactly where it went wrong.

What's new

  • A home screen installed another way is left as it is. Some TVs already had the new home screen from the Clean Your TV tool for computers, which signs it with a different key. Setup used to stop with "plan refused" on every try. Now it leaves that home screen as it is and does the clean-up (#171, #187, #220).
  • An honest message when there is no safe plan. Setup used to say "We couldn't read what's on the TV" even though the TV had answered. Now it says it couldn't make a plan it is sure is safe, that nothing was changed, and Report a problem sends us the reason (#82, #99, #45).
  • Manage explains it too. On those TVs, Home screen says Setup left the home screen as it was, instead of offering a dock and a look for it.
  • Reports name the reason. The diagnostics log now says why a plan was refused. Apps you installed yourself are never named.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.3.3 fixes the issues people reported on the app's first public day. Thank you all: every report made this release better.

What's new

  • A TV that keeps something on no longer stops Setup. Some TVs answer "yes" when the app switches an app off, then keep it on. Setup now skips it, runs the rest of the clean-up, and Done names what wouldn't switch off. Before, Carry on met the same step again every time (#10).
  • Your own launcher is safe. A launcher you installed yourself is never switched off. If the TV's home screen was already changed, by another app or an earlier change, Setup leaves it as it is and does the clean-up, instead of "plan refused" (#8).
  • Honest Done screens. When nothing was changed, Done says so, and why (#15).
  • Manage explains the home screen. On a TV that kept its own home screen, Manage says why and what would change it, instead of a dock and a look that ended in "We stopped" (#3).
  • Reports fill the form in for you. Help add this TV and Report a problem now put the report straight into the GitHub form, and the report box can't be posted empty (#12, #14, #16).
  • Build numbers like "V816.0.11.0" are no longer masked as network addresses in reports.

items.summary: Clean Your TV app 0.3.2 fixes the first issues people reported, and makes it easy to report a problem or a TV the app doesn't know yet. Thank you to everyone who took the time to write in. What's new Fire TV sets are recognised on their own. Fire TV and Fire…
items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.3.2 fixes the first issues people reported, and makes it easy to report a problem or a TV the app doesn't know yet. Thank you to everyone who took the time to write in.

What's new

  • Fire TV sets are recognised on their own. Fire TV and Fire TV Edition TVs (Insignia, Toshiba and others) are now recognised from the TV's own details, even when the app has no list for the exact model. They get the clean-up only: Fire OS doesn't let another home screen take over, so the app no longer tries (#2).
  • Undo can't get stuck any more. Undo now checks the TV itself: if the TV's own home screen is back, undo is done, even when the TV refuses a step that is already in place. If 0.3.1 left you on "The setup didn't finish", it clears the next time the app connects to the TV after updating.
  • A way out, always. Stop here shows Done only once the run has really stopped, and "Forget this TV" ends an unfinished setup for that TV.
  • Help add this TV. When the app doesn't know your TV yet, one tap makes a short report of what the TV is and which apps it came with. Apps you installed yourself are only counted, never named. You read the whole text first, then paste it into a pre-filled GitHub form or share it another way. The app sends nothing itself (#1).
  • Report a problem, in Settings and on the screens where something went wrong, does the same with the app's log. The log is now readable: plain error names, how the TV was matched, and the step that failed with the TV's answer.
  • Privacy: the policy now describes these reports and the app's own log, which "Delete everything" also clears. Nothing new is collected.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

Install

items.summary: The first public release of Clean Your TV app, a community-built phone app for Clean Your TV. Anyone can now clean up an Android TV, Google TV or Fire TV from an Android phone: no laptop, no coding agent, no cables. The app switches off adverts, tracking and…
items.html:
The first public release of Clean Your TV app, a community-built phone app for Clean Your TV. Anyone can now clean up an Android TV, Google TV or Fire TV from an Android phone: no laptop, no coding agent, no cables. The app switches off adverts, tracking and preloaded apps, installs the calm Clean Your TV home screen with a dock of the apps you use, shows its progress on the TV, and keeps a restore point so every change can be put back.

Highlights

  • 131 community tested TV profiles from 46 brands, plus a careful brand fallback for models nobody has profiled yet.
  • Launcher 2.5 (upstream v2.5.0): edit the dock from the remote, rows and wallpaper in Launcher settings, and more. A dock changed on the TV survives a new look from the phone.
  • A plan first. See what will be switched off and what is kept; Customise shows every command in order before it runs.
  • Restore point and undo, one app or everything, plus a restore copy with plain scripts that work from any computer with adb.
  • A watchdog on the TV puts its own home screen back if the phone does not confirm the new one within 150 seconds.
  • Stricter safety: the app never switches off what drives the HDMI and tuner inputs, accessibility or the remote, and on TVs where switching the home screen is known to cause trouble (Chromecast with Google TV, the Google TV Streamer, some Kalley and PRISM+ sets, TVs whose setup wizard must stay on) it does the clean-up only and says why.
  • No accounts, no analytics; internet only to GitHub, and only when you ask.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

Install
